_comment: The canonical claim is a real invoice in a real accounting system, read back through an
authenticated call. Variants are the SAME claim rewritten the way a second lender would
receive it. Every canonical value was returned by the provider; none was invented.
The negative control is a SECOND REAL INVOICE, not a variant. The original entry here only
changed the invoice number, which made it agree on six of seven components — exactly what a
legitimate reformatting scores — so no threshold could separate them. That entry was not a
negative control at all: it was the near-collision squatting attack wearing one.
issuerTaxId is the ledger tenant id. The organisation's own tax number would need a settings
scope this connection does not hold, and reconnecting days before a deadline risks the only
accounting credential that exists. The tenant id is real, stable, and already known to the
enclave. debtorTaxId falls back to the canonical debtor NAME when the ledger carries no tax
number, which is the case for 82 of this ledger's 83 contacts.

variants.label: amount written with a decimal separator
a second real invoice: different debtor, number, amount bucket and due date
variants._provenance: Seeded through the real API against contact ef6f54c1; the debtor has no tax number so its identity is the canonical name.

measured._amountIsFaceValue: Total including tax. For both invoices here the total and the outstanding balance coincide because both are unpaid.
